artists.biography:
Ben Folds Five is an alternative rock trio formed in 1993 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. The group comprises Ben Folds (lead vocals, piano, keyboards, melodica, principal songwriting), Robert Sledge (bass, contrabass, synthesizer, backing vocals), and Darren Jessee (drums, percussion, backing vocals, co-writer for some songs). The group achieved mainstream success in the alternative, indie and pop music scenes. The band is best known for the hit single "Brick" from their 1997 album Whatever and Ever Amen, which gained airplay on many mainstream radio stations.

Much of Ben Folds Five's work was influenced by jazz, evident in frequent improv-styled passages through bridge and/or ending. During their seven years together, the band released three proper studio records, one retrospective album of B-sides and outtakes, and eight singles. They also contributed to a number of soundtracks and compilations. Ben Folds Five disbanded in October 2000, apparently under amicable circumstances.

The group reunited for a one-off concert on September 18, 2008, where they played their final album, The Unauthorized Biography of Reinhold Messner, in its entirety. In 2011, Ben Folds Five reunited to record three tracks for Ben Folds' The Best Imitation of Myself: A Retrospective. It was announced on Folds' Twitter in January of 2012 that the band has reunited to record a new album. As of March 1 of the same year, at least three tour dates have been added, including the Bonnaroo festival in Manchester, Tennessee, DeLuna Festival in Pensacola, Florida, and the Mountain Jam Festival in Hunter, NY.  

In July of 2012 the band announced US and European tour dates for Fall 2012.

perplexity.description:
Ben Folds Five, released in 1995 on Caroline Records (not Plain Recordings), is the self-titled debut album by the American alternative rock trio Ben Folds Five. The album showcases the band’s distinctive sound, built around Ben Folds’ energetic piano playing, Robert Sledge’s melodic bass lines, and Darren Jessee’s dynamic drumming. Musically, the record blends elements of rock, pop, and indie sensibilities, with Folds’ witty, often introspective lyrics and a style that mixes ’70s AM radio harmonies with a ’90s college rock edge. Notable tracks include “Underground,” “Where’s Summer B.?,” “Alice Childress,” and “Jackson Cannery,” each highlighting the band’s knack for catchy melodies and clever songwriting.

As the first full-length statement from Ben Folds Five, the album established the trio’s unique identity in the alternative rock scene and set the stage for their subsequent success. While it did not chart upon release, the album’s critical acclaim and underground popularity led to a major-label bidding war, ultimately resulting in the band signing with Sony Music. Ben Folds Five remains a foundational work in the band’s discography, marking the beginning of Ben Folds’ influential career and paving the way for their breakthrough with the 1997 follow-up, Whatever and Ever Amen.
